propositions: Phase 2 verification lacks a check for whether asserted harms are reachable via concrete triggering inputs or states, allowing plausible but unreachable proposals to pass unflagged
Phase 3 remediation proposers operate on identical evidence and measure prompt stability rather than correctness; blind parallelism requires decorrelated priors to achieve meaningful convergence
Proposals that reverse recorded deliberate project decisions lack validation that the evidence supporting the decision has changed, permitting reversals to enter Phase 4 approval uncontested

The validity scoring formula must incorporate reachability of harm as a fifth binary sub-question with a -0.10 penalty when a finding reverses an explicitly justified prior decision without naming changed evidence

Phase 3 proposers must be asymmetric: Proposer A researches OSS practice while Proposer B consults project history (tickets, ADRs, git log/blame); divergent moves trigger research into community and project adoption patterns before emitting plan items
